page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features a single dedicated vCPU mapped to an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 4:1. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of the n1-standard-1 in the lower tiers. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, yields a score of 1088.79, categorizing it in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.25 GB/sec for cached small blocks and drop to 10.68 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Other performance metrics, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 895.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 1262.29, reflect limited processing capabilities.

Due to its entry-level hardware profile and lower-tier benchmark results, the n1-standard-1 is suited for lightweight, non-resource-intensive workloads. These include basic static web serving, which achieves a throughput of 1.21 GB/sec, small Redis database instances handling up to 1.29 million SET operations per second, and minor text or image processing tasks. It is not designed for demanding database operations, large-scale LLM inference, or multi-threaded applications.
